scope: Repair the current dependency-seam blocker by authorizing the app-shell frontend prototype's mock-only render-envelope serde/serde_json boundary, while proving the local dev-server JSON envelope path and preserving no-backend/no-production claims.
claim: The dependency-rationales registry now narrowly allowlists oya-application-shell-frontend-prototype for serde and serde_json only at the mock render-envelope DTO/local dev-server-to-WASM boundary. Current dependency-seam passes; app-shell package checks/tests/clippy pass in default and SSR configurations; oya-check-dependency-seam tests/clippy pass. After the separately recorded workflow-cohesion evidence metadata normalization, ./bin/oya gate run-all --ci-required passes 88/88 lanes. Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is still not claimed until the wrapper is rerun end-to-end. Dependency-seam app-shell serde policy repair plus workflow metadata normalization now sits under a full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required PASS.

pre_repair_failures.summary: dependency-seam failed with 4 blocking diagnostics because oya-application-shell-frontend-prototype declared/imported serde and serde_json outside the allowed_crates lists.

Initial RED guard referenced a helper that did not exist; current source already exposed render_envelope_json, so the guard was adjusted to prove the existing endpoint serializer instead of inventing a second helper.

Current app-shell source had clippy::too_many_arguments diagnostics in prototype view functions; SSR clippy also found a needless return in render_envelope.rs. These were fixed without changing runtime semantics. The overwritten green gate log and terminal transcript capture the final state.
First provider-admission attempt failed in Trivy SARIF emission with a walk-dir error on test-results while that directory was being materialized; rerun passed without source changes.

implemented_changes: Added oya-application-shell-frontend-prototype to the serde allowed_crates list and updated the rationale to name the mock render-envelope DTO boundary explicitly.

Added oya-application-shell-frontend-prototype to the serde_json allowed_crates list and updated the layer/rationale to limit the exception to the local dev-server-to-WASM render-envelope boundary with no PHI/PII/production tenant data and no production backend/API readiness claim.
Added a dependency-seam unit invariant that the live registry explicitly authorizes the app-shell prototype for both serde and serde_json, making accidental removal visible in package tests.

Added SSR dev-server render-envelope tests proving the current serializer emits one permitted TenantRenderEnvelope, rejects unknown contexts, and does not leak the server-only mock catalog sentinel or Clinical Home module into an unaccredited tenant-admin envelope.
Added localized clippy expectations for high-arity Leptos prototype view functions and removed a needless return in the SSR render-envelope selector.

remaining_blockers: No known mandatory local verify blocker remains in the final observed run; future runs must still reverify because concurrent agents are active.
non_claims: No production backend/API readiness, real auth/authz, live frontend deployment, PHI/PII handling, provider-live operation, measured SLO, DR, sharding, compliance certification, or hyperscaler readiness is claimed.

A live-registry unit invariant prevents silent removal or accidental under-documentation of this explicit exception.
Dependency-seam is green again on current source, but the evidence explicitly refuses production/hyperscaler readiness claims.

dependency-seam red evidence captured the exact blocked serde/serde_json diagnostics before the allowlist repair.
Future contributors can read dependency-rationales.json to see why the app-shell prototype is the only frontend exception for serde_json.

Targeted tests, package clippy, app-shell default/SSR gates, formatting, and dependency-seam all pass after the repair.

alternatives_named: Remove serde/serde_json from the app shell again
Allowlist only serde and hand-roll JSON parsing
Narrowly allowlist serde and serde_json for the existing mock render-envelope boundary
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The current source intentionally serializes a typed TenantRenderEnvelope between the SSR dev server and selective WASM island; a narrow allowlist plus tests matches source truth and avoids racing concurrent rewrites.
rejected_reasons: Repeated removal was already undone by concurrent dashboard edits and no longer represented current source truth.
Hand-rolled JSON parsing would be lower quality and riskier than serde_json for a typed prototype DTO, without improving production readiness.

findings: The serializer/deserializer path is mock-only and uses static INTERNAL_ONLY envelope data, not untrusted production tenant data or PHI/PII.
The SSR test proves the server-only catalog sentinel is not emitted in the tenant-admin envelope JSON.
No performance-sensitive runtime path is claimed; serde_json is used only in the local prototype render-envelope exchange.
No benchmark or SLO claim is made.
The exception is documented as no PHI/PII/production tenant data and no compliance certification claim.
Audit-chain evidence is recorded for the policy repair.
